blocks.title: Automation and Scripting Use Cases comparison
Automation and Scripting Use Cases exam shortcuts
items: New hire accounts created automatically → USER PROVISIONING
Automate identity setup and standard access.
Example: HR entry triggers email and application account creation.
Cloud environment built from approved templates → RESOURCE PROVISIONING
Automate infrastructure deployment.
Example: A script creates a VM, subnet, and security settings.
Bad configuration must be blocked before deployment → GUARD RAIL
Prevent insecure changes automatically.
Example: A policy blocks creation of a public storage bucket.
Security alert should create work for IT → TICKET CREATION
Convert detections into trackable work items.
Example: SIEM opens a remediation ticket.
Critical alert needs senior analyst immediately → ESCALATION
Automatically increase priority or route ownership.
Example: A high-severity detection is sent to Tier 2.
Compromised account should lose access automatically → DISABLE ACCESS
Automation can contain incidents quickly.
Example: IAM disables a user after confirmed compromise.
Need security checks on every code change → CI / TESTING
Embed automated security testing into the pipeline.
Example: Static analysis runs on every pull request.
Two security tools must exchange data/actions → API / INTEGRATION
Use APIs to connect systems.
Example: SOAR pulls indicators from threat intelligence and updates the firewall.
blocks.example: First identify whether the scenario is describing an automation use case, a benefit, or an operational drawback.

questions.q: HR adds a new employee and an automated workflow creates the user's email and application accounts. Which use case is this?
questions.explanation: User provisioning automates creation and configuration of user accounts and access.

questions.q: A script creates a new cloud VM, subnet, and storage resource from an approved template. Which use case is this?
questions.explanation: Resource provisioning automates deployment of infrastructure and services.

questions.q: A cloud policy automatically blocks creation of publicly accessible storage buckets. Which automation use case is this?
questions.explanation: Guard rails prevent insecure or noncompliant configurations from being deployed.

questions.q: A SIEM automatically opens an incident in the ticketing system when a critical alert fires. Which use case is this?
questions.explanation: Ticket creation converts security events into trackable work items.

questions.q: A high-severity alert is automatically routed from Tier 1 to a senior analyst. Which use case is this?
questions.explanation: Escalation automatically raises priority or routes an issue to a higher support level.

questions.q: A confirmed compromised account is automatically disabled. Which use case is this?
questions.explanation: Automation can enable or disable services, accounts, or access based on policy or events.

questions.q: Static analysis and configuration checks run automatically on every code change. Which use case is this?
questions.explanation: CI/testing automates validation on every software or configuration change.

questions.q: A SOAR platform sends indicators to a firewall and retrieves threat intelligence from another system. What enables this automation?
questions.explanation: APIs and integrations allow tools to exchange data and trigger actions.
